verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华啊，我曾求告你，求你快快临到我这里！我求告你的时候，愿你留心听我的声音！
verses.en: A psalm of David.O Lord, I cry out to you. Come quickly to me.Pay attention to me when I cry out to you.

verses.zh: 愿我的祷告如香陈列在你面前！愿我举手祈求，如献晚祭！
verses.en: May you accept my prayer like incense,my uplifted hands like the evening offering.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 141. The psalmist asks God to protect him from sin and from sinful men.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你禁止我的口，把守我的嘴！
verses.en: O Lord, place a guard on my mouth.Protect the opening[NOTE:1] of my lips.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “may my prayer be established [like] incense before you, the uplifting of my hands [like] an evening offering.”
Heb “door.” The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT.

verses.zh: 求你不叫我的心偏向邪恶，以致我和作孽的人同行恶事；也不叫我吃他们的美食。
verses.en: Do not let me have evil desires[NOTE:1] or participate in sinful activitieswith men who behave wickedly.[NOTE:2] I will not eat their delicacies.[NOTE:3]
notes: My mouth…my lips. The psalmist asks God to protect him from speaking inappropriately or sinfully.
Heb “do not turn my heart toward an evil thing.”
Heb “to act sinfully in practices in wickedness with men, doers of evil.”

verses.zh: 任凭义人击打我，这算为仁慈；任凭他责备我，这算为头上的膏油；我的头不要躲闪。正在他们行恶的时候，我仍要祈祷。
verses.en: May the godly strike me in love and correct me.May my head not refuse[NOTE:1] choice oil.[NOTE:2] Indeed, my prayer is a witness against their evil deeds.[NOTE:3]
notes: Their delicacies. This probably refers to the enjoyment that a sinful lifestyle appears to offer.

The form יָנִי (yani) appears to be derived from the verbal root נוּא (nuʾ). Another option is to emend the form to יְנָא (yenaʾ), a Piel from נָאָה (naʾah), and translate “may choice oil not adorn my head” (see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 271). In this case, choice oil, like delicacies in v. 4, symbolize the pleasures of sin.
May my head not refuse choice oil. The psalmist compares the constructive criticism of the godly (see the previous line) to having refreshing olive oil poured over one’s head.

verses.zh: 他们的审判官被扔在岩下；众人要听我的话，因为这话甘甜。
verses.en: They will be thrown over the side of a cliff by their judges.[NOTE:1] They[NOTE:2] will listen to my words, for they are pleasant.
notes: Heb “for still, and my prayer [is] against their evil deeds.” The syntax of the Hebrew text is difficult; the sequence -כִּי־עוֹד וּ (ki ʿod u-, “for still and”) occurs only here. The translation assumes an emendation to כִּי עֵד תְּפִלָּתִי (ki ʿed tefillati, “indeed a witness [is] my prayer”). The psalmist’s lament about the evil actions of sinful men (see v. 4) testifies against the wicked in the divine court.

Heb “they are thrown down by the hands of a cliff, their judges.” The syntax of the Hebrew text is difficult and the meaning uncertain. The perfect verbal form is understood as rhetorical; the psalmist describes the anticipated downfall of the wicked as if it had already occurred. “Their judges” could be taken as the subject of the verb, but this makes little, if any, sense. The translation assumes the judges are the agents and that the wicked, mentioned earlier in the psalm, are the subjects of the verb.

verses.zh: 我们的骨头散在墓旁，好像人耕田、刨地的土块。
verses.en: As when one plows and breaks up the soil,[NOTE:1] so our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
notes: It is unclear how this statement relates to the preceding sentence. Perhaps the judges are the referent of the pronominal subject (“they”) of the verb “will listen,” and “my words” are the referent of the pronominal subject (“they”) of the phrase “are pleasant.” The psalmist may be affirming here his confidence that he will be vindicated when he presents his case before the judges, while the wicked will be punished.

verses.zh: 主―耶和华啊，我的眼目仰望你；我投靠你，求你不要将我撇得孤苦！
verses.en: Surely I am looking to you,[NOTE:1] O Sovereign Lord.In you I take shelter.Do not expose me to danger.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “like splitting and breaking open in the earth.” The meaning of the statement and the point of the comparison are not entirely clear. Perhaps the psalmist is suggesting that he and other godly individuals are as good as dead; their bones are scattered about like dirt that is dug up and tossed aside.

verses.zh: 求你保护我脱离恶人为我设的网罗和作孽之人的圈套！
verses.en: Protect me from the snare they have laid for meand the traps the evildoers have set.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “do not lay bare my life.” Only here is the Piel form of the verb collocated with the term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “life”). In Isa 53:12 the Lord’s servant “lays bare (the Hiphil form of the verb is used) his life to death.”

verses.zh: 愿恶人落在自己的网里，我却得以逃脱。
verses.en: Let the wicked fall[NOTE:1] into their[NOTE:2] own nets,while I escape.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and the traps of the doers of evil.”
The prefixed verbal form is understood as a jussive of prayer. Another option is to translate, “the wicked will fall.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT
PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in
the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one
and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This Psalm is set during an evening worship time in the temple (Ps. 141:2).

- Like Psalms 139 and 140, this Psalm uses a legal terminology.

- let the psalmist not speak (Ps. 141:3)

- the wicked are both (Ps. 141:6)

- judges

- witnesses

- The imagery of hunting (i.e., often used as military imagery) is again applied to the psalmist's persecutors (cf. Ps. 140:4-5).

- the trap, Ps. 141:9a

- the snares, Ps. 141:9b

- nets, Ps. 141:10a

- This Psalm is dominated by prayer requests (IMPERATIVES/JUSSIVES).

- for the psalmist

- hasten to me, Ps. 141:1a ‒ BDB 301, KB 300, Qal IMPERATIVE

- give ear, Ps. 141:1b ‒ BDB 24, KB 27, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- may my prayer be counted, Ps. 141:2a ‒ BDB 465, KB 464, Niphal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- set a guard over my mouth, Ps. 141:3a ‒ BDB 1011, KB 1483, Qal IMPERATIVE

- keep watch over the door of my lips, Ps. 141:3b ‒ BDB 665, KB 718, Qal
IMPERATIVE; the word "door" (BDB 194) appears only here in the OT

- do not incline my heart to any evil thing, Ps. 141:4a ‒ BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil
JUSSIVE

- let the righteous smite me in kindness, Ps. 41:5a ‒ BDB 240, KB 249, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- let the righteous reprove me, Ps. 141:5a ‒ BDB 406, KB 410, Hiphil IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- do not let my head refuse it, Ps. 141:5c ‒ BDB 626, KB 677, Hiphil IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

- do not leave me defenseless, Ps. 141:8b ‒ BDB 788, KB 881, Piel JUSSIVE

- keep me from the jaws of the trap, Ps. 141:9a ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERATIVE

- let me pass by safely, Ps. 141:10b ‒ BDB 716, KB 778, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense

- for the wicked

- my prayer is against their wicked deeds

(1) throw down their judges, Ps. 141:6a

(2) bones scattered at the mouth of Sheol, Ps. 141:7b

- let the wicked fall into their own nets, Ps. 141:9b - BDB 656, KB 709, Qal
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense sense (i.e., role reversal)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 141:1-4

1O
Lord, I call upon You; hasten to me!

Give ear to my voice when I
call to You!

2May my prayer be
counted as incense before You;

The lifting up of my hands as
the evening offering.

3Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth;

Keep watch over the door of my
lips.

4Do not incline my
heart to any evil thing,

To practice deeds of
wickedness

With men who do iniquity;

And do not let me eat of their
delicacies.

141:1 "O Lord" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "give ear" This is a way of asking for God to be attentive to the psalmist's prayers. God does
not have a physical body.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

141:2a Verses like this in Psalms have allowed Judaism to assert that their worship (i.e., without a temple and,
therefore, no possible sacrifices) is acceptable to YHWH. Prayer and praise are now the sacrifices.

141:2b "lifting up of my hands" This was the normal position of Jewish prayers.

- standing

- head up (i.e., looking to God)

- hand raised (i.e., as if receiving)

- eyes open (i.e., a dialogue with God)

▣ "the evening offering" Part of the sacrificial system was an offering of a lamb in the
temple every morning at 9 AM (cf. Ps. 5:3) and evening at 3 PM (cf. Exod. 29:38-46; Num. 28:1-8).
These offerings were called "The Continual." This became a special time of prayer (i.e., Acts 3:1; 10:30).

141:3 One wonders what the intent of this verse is.

- court scene

- gossip

- verbal attack on persecutors

Notice the two parallel Qal IMPERATIVES
("set a guard," "keep watch over"). Speech reveals the heart.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

141:3b "the door" The Hebrew root דל (BDB 194, KB 221) occurs only here
in the Hebrew Bible. It is parallel to "over my mouth." Therefore, it is imagery for human speech. What
we say matters! It reveals our heart and spiritual orientation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SPEECH

141:4a This verse is a recognition of the sovereignty of God. Moderns must be careful of immediately
seeing this in terms of the Calvinist and Arminian debate (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: PREDESTINATION [Calvinism] vs. HUMAN FREE WILL [Arminianism]).

This reflects the Hebrew worldview. Their God controls all
things (cf. Eccl. 7:14; Isa. 45:7; Lam. 3:38; Amos 3:6b). Statements such as
this are not to be taken as voiding free will or the need for human actions but
a recognition of the one true God (i.e., all causality attributed to God, no
secondary causes; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ONE CAUSALITY).

The VERB "incline" (BDB 639, KB 692,
Hiphil JUSSIVE) is used in a covenant sense in 1 Kgs. 8:58; Ps. 119:36. For a good
parallel to this see Prov. 1:8-19. The desires of the heart reveal the true person.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

141:4b There is true evil (BDB 948) and
rebellion in the world. The faithful follower flees from it and those who
practice it.

141:4d "do not let me eat of their delicacies"
This is another IMPERFECT that is used in a
JUSSIVE sense. It is uncertain if this refers to

- a social event

- sinful lifestyle

- idolatrous worship setting; it is possible both Psalm 139 and 140 are related to discussions of idolatry

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 141:5-7

5Let the righteous
smite me in kindness and reprove me;

It is oil upon the head;

Do not let my head refuse it,

For still my prayer is against
their wicked deeds.

6Their judges are
thrown down by the sides of the rock,

And they hear my words, for
they are pleasant.

7As when one plows
and breaks open the earth,

Our bones have been scattered
at the mouth of Sheol.

141:5 This verse reflects a recurrent theme in Proverbs (cf. Prov. 9:8; 19:25; 25:12;
also note Eccl. 7:5). Instruction and correction from a righteous person are treasured gifts to those
who have God's wisdom.

Psalm 141:5 has three IMPERFECTS used in a
JUSSIVE sense.

- smite ‒ BDB 240, 249, Qal IMPERFECT

- reprove ‒ BDB 406, KB 410, Hiphil IMPERFECT

- refuse ‒ BDB 626, KB 677, Hiphil IMPERFECT

▣ "in kindness" This is the important covenant term, hesed. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed).

▣ "It is oil upon the head" The NRSV, TEV, NJB, and REB follow the LXX, "but let
not the sinner's oil anoint my head." Psalm 141:5-7 is very difficult in Hebrew. There are many divergent
translations. The NRSV, TEV, and JPSOA have footnotes which say that Ps. 141:5,6,7 are uncertain. Best to
get the general sense and move on to the next strophe!

For textual variants, see UBS Text Project, pp. 431-434.

141:5d The last poetic line seems out of place in relation to the first four lines. The NKJV starts
the next strophe (Ps. 141:5f-7) with it.

141:6 "the rock" This may be

- a reference to their deaths (cf. 2 Chr. 25:12)

- a title for YHWH (i.e., "the Rock," cf. Deut. 32:18; Ps. 18:2,31,46; 19:14; 28:1; 31:3; 42:9; 71:3;
see NAB and NJB translations)

- a reference to the temple mount

141:7 "the mouth of Sheol" The OT
holding place of the dead was personified as an animal that devoured>

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 141:8-10

8For my eyes are
toward You, O God, the Lord;

In You I take refuge; do not
leave me defenseless.

9Keep me from the
jaws of the trap which they have set for me,

And from the snares of those
who do iniquity.

10Let the wicked
fall into their own nets,

While I pass by safely.

141:8a This is the psalmist's affirmation of faith in the covenant God of Israel. For
"YHWH" (God) and "Adon" (Lord).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (Adon and Kurios)

141:8b "refuge" This is a common VERB (BDB 340, KB 337, Qal PERFECT)
in the Psalter. See notes at Ps. 2:12 online (www.freebiblecommentary.org).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE

▣ "do not leave me defenseless" The second VERB (BDB 788, KB 881, Piel
JUSSIVE) basically means "to be naked" or "to be bare" (i.e., exposed). BDB and KB assert that here,
and here only, it means "poured out" (which has a sacrificial connotation, see Hiphil form in Isa. 53:12).

▣ "me" This is the Hebrew nephesh
(BDB 659), which denoted the entire person. See note at Gen. 35:18 online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

141:9-10 This is imagery from Israel's
hunting techniques, see notes at Ps. 140:4-5.

- the trap (BDB 809)

- the snares (BDB 430)

- nets (BDB 485, found only here but another word for "net" [BDB 440] is found in Ps. 140:5)

141:10 "Let the wicked fall into their own nets" Humans reap what they sow! This is a biblical
principle stated so often (cf. Job 34:11; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:29;
Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17;
Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12). This is a moral creation. We do not break God's law; we break ourselves on them.

▣ "While I pass by safely" This verse expresses the expected outcome of the "two ways"
(cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30:15,19; Psalm 1).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide
commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of
the Bible. Each of us must walk n the light we have. You, the Bible, and the
Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a
commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think
through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought provoking, not definitive.

- Why is Ps. 141:2 so important to Judaism?

- Do Ps. 141:3 and 4 support predestination?

- To what does Ps. 141:4d refer?

- Is Ps. 141:5-7 all about the wicked?

- What does "the rock" in Ps. 141:6a mean?

- Define "the two ways." How does Ps. 141:10 reference this OT theological assumption?
